topic: Hubble launched with a blurry mirror (1990)
claim: Hubble's main mirror was ground about 2.2 microns (roughly 1/50 of a human hair) too flat at its edge because its test device was set up wrong; astronauts installed corrective optics (COSTAR, WFPC2) in December 1993.

beats.caption: Hubble launched blurry
beats.vo: Hubble launched with a blurry mirror.

beats.caption: 2.2 microns off
beats.vo: The mirror was ground wrong by just 2.2 microns. That's about one fiftieth of a human hair.

beats.caption: A test set up wrong
beats.vo: The test device used to shape it was set up wrong. One lens spacing was off by 1.3 millimeters.

beats.caption: NASA finds the flaw
beats.vo: Two months after launch, on June 27th, 1990, NASA announced the flaw. Stars looked fuzzy.

beats.caption: Glasses for Hubble
beats.vo: Astronauts couldn't swap the mirror. So in December 1993, they installed corrective optics. Tiny mirrors that work like glasses.

beats.caption: Sharp ever since
beats.vo: Every new instrument since has the fix built in. Hubble has seen sharp ever since.

sources.text: NASA Science, The History of Hubble: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/overview/the-history-of-hubble/
